CORE PRINCIPLE: SINE AND COSINE ARE CIRCLE COORDINATES
Textbook right triangles only work for angles < 90°. The volvelle proves that sine and
are the literal (X, Y) coordinates of a point moving around a circle! In Quadrant II, cosine
naturally becomes negative because X is negative, while sine remains positive!
Rotate cursor to 60°. Notice X and Y coordinates swap: X = cos(60°) = 1/2 = 0.500, Y =
